item.title: Cath
item.description:
Cath (${⌾}$) refers to two distinct concepts within Kittens Game: the name of the solar system where the game takes place, and a specific five-year astrological cycle.

1. The Cath Solar System

Cath is the name of the solar system in which the star Helios resides, which is a G2V spectral type star at the system’s centre. The core resources of the game, such as unobtainium, are produced on planets or satellites within the Cath solar system.
item.content:encoded:
Cath (${⌾}$) refers to two distinct concepts within Kittens Game: the name of the solar system where the game takes place, and a specific five-year astrological cycle.

1. The Cath Solar System

Cath is the name of the solar system in which the star Helios resides, which is a G2V spectral type star at the system’s centre. The core resources of the game, such as unobtainium, are produced on planets or satellites within the Cath solar system.

2. The Cath Astrological Cycle

Cath is one of the ten planetary cycles in the time system, with each cycle lasting five years. It is identified by the glyph ${⌾}$. The effects of this cycle are only triggered once the Numerology upgrade has been researched.

Category Detail
Duration 5 years
Glyph ${⌾}$

Effects with Numerology:

When the Cath cycle is active, it provides several bonuses and a specific penalty related to space structures:

  • Space Elevator transfer production bonus (for oil only): Increased by $+100%$. The Space Elevator structure also has its conversion production (resources produced by Smelters, Calciners, and Accelerators) on Cath boosted by a bonus of $0.4%$ per leader rank per uncapped population buildings.
  • Satellite starchart production: Increased by $+100%$.
  • Satellite observatory’s science bonus: Increased by $+100%$.
  • Space Station science bonus: Increased by $+50%$.
  • Space Beacon starchart production: Decreased by $-50%$.

Festival Effect with Numeromancy:

If the advanced Numeromancy upgrade is researched, holding a festival during the Cath cycle grants a significant $\times 2$ multiplier to Catpower income.

Unlocks Successful completion unlocks the Charon Planet.

2. Charon Astrological Cycle

Charon (${⍙}$) is one of the ten planetary cycles, each lasting five years. Its effects are triggered upon researching advanced Metaphysics upgrades:

  • With Numerology: The cycle negatively impacts specific structures related to Unobtainium (UO) and gigaflops:
    • Lunar Outpost unobtainium output is decreased by $-10%$.
    • Entanglement Station gigaflops consumption is increased by $+100%$.
  • Festival Effect (With Numeromancy): If a festival is held during the Charon cycle, it provides a $\times 1.5$ multiplier to Catnip, Wood, and Mineral income.

The severe penalty to Lunar Outpost production during the Charon cycle is notable, especially when compared to the highly advantageous Redmoon cycle, which boosts UO production by $+20%$. Due to this, strategies often revolve around skipping non-profitable cycles, like Charon, using time manipulation.

item.title: Dune
item.description:

1. Dune Space Mission Details

Dune is described as a large, lifeless planet covered by sand and volcanic rock. The Dune Mission is unlocked after successfully completing the Moon Mission.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Moon Mission
Cost 1000 Starchart, 7000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene
Travel Time 356 game-days (11 minutes, 52 seconds in real-time)
Unlocks Helios mission

2. Key Structures and Policy/ Unlocked

Successful completion of the mission unlocks the Dune Planet and critical infrastructure:
item.content:encoded:
Dune (${⍫}$) is a pivotal mid-to-late-game space destination, a planet in the Cath solar system, which unlocks new industrial structures and is tied to a specific astrological cycle that boosts uranium production.

1. Dune Space Mission Details

Dune is described as a large, lifeless planet covered by sand and volcanic rock. The Dune Mission is unlocked after successfully completing the Moon Mission.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Moon Mission
Cost 1000 Starchart, 7000 Titanium, 175k Science, and 75 Kerosene
Travel Time 356 game-days (11 minutes, 52 seconds in real-time)
Unlocks Helios mission

2. Key Structures and Policy/ Unlocked

Successful completion of the mission unlocks the Dune Planet and critical infrastructure:

  • Planet Cracker: A vessel that generates Uranium (1.5/sec). Building this structure requires a significant investment in Starcharts: 1000 Starchart to reach Dune, and 2500 Starchart to build the cracker itself.
  • Hydraulic Fracturer: A structure that produces Oil (2.5/sec). Hydraulic Fracturers are generally not particularly effective until the Space Manufacturing upgrade is secured.
  • Spice Refinery: Refines Dune sand into ‘Spice’ at a rate of 0.125/sec.

Reaching Dune is also a prerequisite for unlocking several high-level Government Policy/, including Technocracy, Cosmological Libertarianism, and Order of the Stars.

3. Dune Astrological Cycle

Dune (${⍫}$) is one of the ten cycles in the game’s time system, with each cycle lasting five years. The effects of this cycle are leveraged by researching Metaphysics upgrades like Numerology and Numeromancy:

  • With Numerology: The cycle provides significant production bonuses for resources generated on Dune: it increases Planet Cracker uranium output by +10% and Hydraulic Fracturer oil output by +50%. Conversely, it imposes a penalty on HR Harvester Energy Production (-25%).
  • With Numeromancy (Festival Bonus): Holding a festival during the Dune cycle grants a $\times 2$ multiplier to Uranium income.

Travel Time Reduction

This extensive travel time can be significantly reduced through drive upgrades:

  • Base Travel Time: The base travel time for the mission is massive, calculated at 725,200,000 game-days.

Travel Time Reduction

This extensive travel time can be significantly reduced through drive upgrades:

  • If you have researched both the Antimatter Drive and the Thorium Drive, the mission travel time is divided by 75.
  • With both drive upgrades, the travel time is reduced to approximately 223 days, 19 hours, 51 minutes, and 7 seconds in real-time.

Status

Currently, the mission’s unlock is listed as “(TBD)”. As of one source’s reported version (1.4.6.2.b), no structures can be built in the Furthest Ring. However, as of a later version (1.4.8.5), players who are logged in will see a text-based interface when they reach the Furthest Ring.

item.title: Helios

The Helios mission is a significant undertaking that occurs in the mid-to-late game, following the Dune Mission.

Structures Unlocked Successful completion unlocks high-tier structures needed for antimatter and storage capacity: Sunlifter, Containment Chamber, Heatsink, and Sunforge.
Next Mission The Helios Mission unlocks the Yarn Mission.

2. Helios Astrological Cycle

Helios is one of the ten cycles in the time system, identified by the glyph ⌒. Each cycle lasts for five years.

item.title: Lunar Outpost
item.description:
A Lunar Outpost is a space structure essential for late-game progression, specifically for refining uranium into unobtainium.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Lunar Outpost based on the sources:

Primary Function and Resources

The Lunar Outpost serves a single, critical purpose:

  • It refines uranium into unobtainium. Unobtainium is a special resource required to unlock Metaphysics and to purchase high-tier buildings and upgrades, including Unobtainium Huts.
  • Consumption Rate: The Lunar Outpost consumes uranium at a rate of 1.75 per second.
  • Production Rate: It produces unobtainium at a rate of 0.035 per second. This means, at full speed, it can produce 5 unobtainium in 142.8 seconds (about 2.3 minutes).

Acquisition and Prerequisites

The Lunar Outpost is unlocked and built through the Space tab:
item.content:encoded:
A Lunar Outpost is a space structure essential for late-game progression, specifically for refining uranium into unobtainium.

Here is a comprehensive overview of the Lunar Outpost based on the sources:

Primary Function and Resources

The Lunar Outpost serves a single, critical purpose:

  • It refines uranium into unobtainium. Unobtainium is a special resource required to unlock Metaphysics and to purchase high-tier buildings and upgrades, including Unobtainium Huts.
  • Consumption Rate: The Lunar Outpost consumes uranium at a rate of 1.75 per second.
  • Production Rate: It produces unobtainium at a rate of 0.035 per second. This means, at full speed, it can produce 5 unobtainium in 142.8 seconds (about 2.3 minutes).

Acquisition and Prerequisites

The Lunar Outpost is unlocked and built through the Space tab:

  • Prerequisite: You must first research the Rocketry science to enable the Space tab and space missions [5, 6].
  • Mission Requirement: The Lunar Outpost itself is unlocked by completing the Moon Mission.
  • Starchart Cost: To complete the Lunar Outpost mission, you need 650 Starcharts [7]. The total starcharts needed to reach the Lunar Outpost, starting from the Orbital Launch (250) and Moon Mission (500), is 1,400 Starcharts [7].
  • Other Costs: The Moon Mission itself also requires 45K oil [8].

Production Efficiency and Optimization

The Lunar Outpost’s production of unobtainium is noted for its inefficiency relative to its resource consumption, which heavily bottlenecks early unobtainium production:

  • Production Slowdown: If your main source of uranium is a single Accelerator (which produces $0.0125$ uranium per second), the Lunar Outpost will run 140 times slower than its maximum speed [9]. This means it could take 5.3 hours to produce 5 unobtainium, rather than 2.3 minutes [4, 9].
  • Trade Solution: Production can be sped up by trading with Dragons for uranium [9].
  • Redshift Advantage (Offline): The source notes that the “Redshift” mechanic, which prevents resources from being deliberately reduced during offline progression, effectively allows Lunar Outposts to run as if you have infinite uranium while offline. This significantly speeds up unobtainium gain during offline progress because the outpost runs at full speed [10].
  • Upgrades: The Microwarp Reactors Workshop upgrade, unlocked by Exometallurgy, makes unobtainium production 75% more effective [11].

Related Space Structures

The Lunar Outpost is key to later resource storage and production:

  • Moon Base: Once you produce 50 unobtainium using the Lunar Outpost, you can build a Moon Base [12]. The Moon Base then increases your overall Unobtainium storage capacity [12, 13].
  • Uranium Consumption: Lunar Outposts initially consume 10 Wt of Energy, although this consumption is reduced by Antimatter Bases [14].

In short, the Lunar Outpost is the specialized factory on the moon that converts titanium-derived uranium into the scarce, late-game resource unobtainium, paving the way for further progression into space and metaphysics [1, 4].

item.title: Piscine
item.description:
Piscine (${⎈}$) refers to a significant destination in the late mid-game space race, resulting in infrastructure critical for advancing scientific research and generating Starcharts. It is also one of the astronomical cycles in the game’s time system.

1. Piscine Space Mission

The Piscine mission targets a gigantic aquatic planet characterised by an acid body and a methane atmosphere.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite Unlocked after successfully completing the Moon Mission.
Cost Requires 1500 Starchart, 9000 Titanium, 200k Science, and 250 Kerosene.
Travel Time 256 game-days (8 minutes, 32 seconds in real-time).
Unlocks Unlocks the Piscine Planet, the Research Vessel building, and the T-minus Mission.

The Pisces Mission is a major investment point, requiring 1500 Starcharts to bypass the starchart bottleneck needed for continued space progression.

Unlocks Unlocks the Piscine Planet, the Research Vessel building, and the T-minus Mission.

The Pisces Mission is a major investment point, requiring 1500 Starcharts to bypass the starchart bottleneck needed for continued space progression.

2. Research Vessel Building

The successful mission unlocks the Research Vessel building, which is crucial for maximizing scientific progress:

  • Science Storage: Each Research Vessel provides a substantial increase of +10,000 maximum Science.
  • Starchart Production: They are highly efficient, generating 0.05 Starchart per second. Research Vessels are considered the most efficient way to acquire Starcharts.

3. Piscine Astrological Cycle

Piscine (${⎈}$) is one of the ten planetary cycles in the time system, each lasting five years.

  • Numerology Effect: With the Numerology upgrade, the Piscine cycle offers contrasting effects on space production:
    • Research Vessel starchart production is boosted by +50%.
    • Hydroponics Catnip Production is decreased by -50%.
  • Festival Effect (Numeromancy): If the Numeromancy upgrade is researched, holding a festival during the Piscine cycle grants a powerful $\times 2$ multiplier to Science income.

The Piscine Mission unlocks Research Vessels, which are essential for boosting science maximums and generating Starcharts efficiently, setting the stage for the next deep space ventures like the T-minus Mission. This allows you to convert high-cost materials into a sustained, high-volume flow of Starcharts needed for future space exploration.

item.title: Redmoon
item.description:

Redmoon is a planet satellite targeted during the mid-to-late game space race:

  • Mission Unlock: The Moon Mission is unlocked after the Orbital Launch and requires 500 Starchart, 5000 Titanium, 125,000 Science, and 45,000 Oil to launch.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Redmoon takes 30 game-days, equivalent to 1 minute in real-time.
  • Unlocks: A successful mission unlocks the Lunar Outpost and the Moon Base structures, as well as the subsequent Dune Mission and Piscine Mission.

2. Buildings on Redmoon

The mission allows for the establishment of two critical structures on Redmoon:
item.content:encoded:
Redmoon (${⍜}$) is both a key destination in the space exploration phase and a recurring astronomical cycle in Kittens Game, offering significant advantages for late-game production, particularly of Unobtainium (UO).

1. Redmoon as a Planetary Mission

Redmoon is a planet satellite targeted during the mid-to-late game space race:

  • Mission Unlock: The Moon Mission is unlocked after the Orbital Launch and requires 500 Starchart, 5000 Titanium, 125,000 Science, and 45,000 Oil to launch.
  • Travel Time: The journey to Redmoon takes 30 game-days, equivalent to 1 minute in real-time.
  • Unlocks: A successful mission unlocks the Lunar Outpost and the Moon Base structures, as well as the subsequent Dune Mission and Piscine Mission.

2. Buildings on Redmoon

The mission allows for the establishment of two critical structures on Redmoon:

  • Lunar Outpost: This nuclear-powered mining outpost is crucial for the Unobtainium economy. It consumes Uranium (at a rate of 1.75/sec) and produces Unobtainium (at 0.035/sec).
  • Moon Base: This base provides large storage increases for core resources, notably providing +45,000 maximum Catnip and +150 maximum Unobtainium storage.

3. Redmoon Astrological Cycle

Redmoon (${⍜}$) is one of the ten astronomical cycles in the game’s time system, with each cycle lasting five years. Its effects are highly advantageous for players who have researched advanced Metaphysics:

  • With Numerology: When the Numerology upgrade is researched, the Redmoon cycle affects specific space production:
    • Lunar Outpost unobtainium output is increased by +20%.
    • Entanglement Station gigaflops consumption is decreased by -50%.
  • Festival Effect (With Numeromancy): If the Numeromancy upgrade is researched, holding a festival during the Redmoon cycle grants a potent $\times 2$ multiplier to Unobtainium income.

Strategic Importance in Endgame

The Redmoon cycle is strategically crucial in the endgame, particularly for advancing the Unobtainium (UO) economy:

  • UO Production: Since Unobtainium is a critical bottleneck resource refined from Uranium by the Lunar Outpost, the Redmoon cycle’s +20% boost to Lunar Outpost output (with Numerology) is highly leveraged.
  • Chrono-Optimization: The Redmoon cycle is part of the Chrono Engine strategy. Using the Chronoforge to shatter Time Crystals (TCs) allows players to skip less profitable periods and arrive at the highly advantageous Redmoon cycle, which provides an instantaneous $2.5\times$ boost to UO production when combined with active Festivals and the Numeromancy upgrade. This strategy converts stored temporal capital (TCs) into a leveraged spike in high-value resource production.
  • Unobtainium Production Formula: If you are always in the Redmoon cycle, the formula for UO production gains an extra factor of $2.4* (1 + 0.01* # Breweries)$ when Numeromancy is researched. Therefore, spending time inside a Redmoon cycle is key for maximising unobtainium production.

item.title: T Minus
item.description:
T-minus (⍝) refers to both a significant deep space mission destination and a recurring astronomical cycle in Kittens Game.

1. T-Minus Space Mission and Structures

The T-minus Mission targets Terminus, a supermassive ice giant at the far end of the Helios solar system.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite The T-minus Mission is unlocked after the Piscine Mission.
Cost 2,500 Starchart, 12,000 Titanium, 225,000 Science, and 750 Kerosene.
Travel Time 2,500 game-days (1 hour, 23 minutes, 20 seconds in real-time).
Unlocks Successful completion unlocks the T-Minus Planet, the Helios Mission, the Kairo Mission, and the Cryostation building.

Cryostation Building: The Cryostation, unlocked by this mission, is a vast storage facility complex that provides significant capacity increases for wood, minerals, iron, coal, uranium, titanium, oil, and unobtainium. Critically, each Cryostation provides $+750$ maximum Unobtainium (UO) storage. UO capacity, specifically from Cryostations and Moon Bases, defines the deep endgame progression toward positive chrono-resets.

item.title: Umbra
item.description:
Umbra refers to both a deep space destination reachable via a mission and a recurring astrological cycle that impacts your production in Kittens Game.

1. Umbra Cycle (Time System)

Umbra is one of the ten cycles featured in the game’s time system, identified by the glyph ${⍦}$. Each cycle lasts for five years.

When the appropriate technologies are researched, the Umbra cycle provides specific bonuses and penalties:

  • With Numerology: The cycle affects production from specific space structures:
    • The uranium output of the Planet Cracker is decreased by $-10%$.
    • The oil output of the Hydraulic Fracturer is decreased by $-25%$.
    • The HR Harvester Energy Production is increased by $+50%$.
  • With Numeromancy (Festival Bonus): Holding a festival during the Umbra cycle grants a $1.5\times$ income multiplier for Coal, Iron, Titanium, and Gold.

2. Umbra Mission and HR Harvester

Umbra is a destination in deep space, described as a supermassive black hole at the heart of the Helios system.

    • 500k Science

  • Travel Time: The journey to Umbra takes 7,600 game-days, equivalent to 4 hours, 13 minutes, and 20 seconds in real-time.

  • Progression: The Umbra Mission subsequently unlocks the Charon Mission.

item.title: Yarn
item.description:

Here is a detailed overview of the Yarn Mission, its costs, and the resulting infrastructure:

Yarn Space Mission

The Yarn Mission targets a Class M planet described as having a high moderate climate, seas, and an oxygen atmosphere.

The Yarn Mission targets a Class M planet described as having a high moderate climate, seas, and an oxygen atmosphere.

Detail Specification
Prerequisite The Yarn Mission is unlocked after the Helios Mission.
Cost 7,500 Starchart, 35,000 Titanium, 350,000 Science, and 12,000 Kerosene.
Travel Time 3,800 game-days (2 hours, 6 minutes, 40 seconds in real-time).
Unlocks Successful completion unlocks the Yarn Planet and the next step in deep space exploration, the Umbra Mission.

Infrastructure Unlocked on Yarn Planet

Completing the mission allows for the construction of two crucial buildings, provided the necessary technologies have been researched:

  1. Terraforming Station: This structure requires the Terraformation research.

    • Cost: 25 Antimatter, 5,000 Uranium, and 5,000 Kerosene.
    • Effect: Increases maximum kitten population by +1.
    • Terraforming Yarn is noted as a necessary action for maximizing housing during deep endgame paragon farming runs.

  2. Hydroponics: This highly efficient agricultural structure requires the Hydroponics technology.

    • Cost: 1 Unobtainium and 500 Kerosene.
    • Effects: Hydroponics provides a +2.5% increase to Catnip Production and increases maximum Catnip Storage capacity by +10%. It also boosts the kitten bonus from the Terraforming Station by $+1.0%$.

Yarn Astrological Cycle

Yarn (${⍧}$) is one of the ten astronomical cycles in the game, each lasting five years. The cycle has specific effects depending on advanced research:

  • With Numerology: The cycle significantly boosts Hydroponics Catnip Production by +100%. However, it imposes a penalty on Research Vessel starchart production, decreasing it by $-50%$.
  • With Numeromancy: If a festival is held during the Yarn cycle, it provides a powerful $\times 2$ multiplier to Culture income.

The Centaurus Mission is a costly undertaking in the latter stages of space exploration:

  • Prerequisite: The mission is unlocked after completing the Rorschach Mission.
  • Cost: Researching and launching the Centaurus Mission requires vast amounts of late-game resources: 100,000 Starchart, 40,000 Titanium, 400,000 Science, 50,000 Kerosene, and 50,000 Thorium.

2. Infrastructure and Challenge Unlock

A successful mission unlocks the Centaurus System and associated buildings:

  • Building Unlocked (Tectonic): The mission enables the construction of the Tectonic structure, provided the player has researched Terraformation. Tectonic is a highly expensive energy production building, costing 600,000 Science, 500 Antimatter, and 75,000 Thorium, and producing 25 Energy.
  • Tectonic Upgrade: The effectiveness of the Tectonic structure can be further improved by the Molten Core upgrade (unlocked by Exophysics), which provides a +5% boost to Tectonic Energy Production per level.
  • Challenge Requirement: Completion of the Centaurus Mission is the specific unlock requirement for the Energy challenge,. The Energy challenge imposes a doubled energy consumption rate on the player’s village,.
